name: Alpenverein-Museum
kurzbeschreibung: The Alpine Club Museum in Innsbruck preserves the most significant collection on the history of alpinism in Austria with over 30,000 historical photographs, alpine art, and pioneering gear.
beschreibung:
Overview

The Alpenverein-Museum of the Austrian Alpine Club (ÖAV) in Innsbruck is Austria's premier museum dedicated to mountaineering and alpinism. It houses an invaluable cultural heritage documenting the exploration of the Alps: the country's largest collection of alpine art (including works by E. T. Compton, Thomas Ender, and Gustav Jahn), some 30,000 historical photographs and glass plate negatives dating back to 1860, pioneering mountaineering equipment, and the central Alpine Archive.

History & Concept

Originating from the Alpine Museum founded in 1911 on Munich's Prater Island, the collections were relocated to Tyrol after World War II. An exhibition space opened in Innsbruck in 1977, and from 2008 to 2014 the museum showed its celebrated permanent exhibition inside the Imperial Hofburg. Today, the museum operates as an innovative "museum on tour" presenting traveling exhibitions across the Alpine region, with archives, depot, and offices based at Olympiastraße 37.

Visit & Getting There

The Olympiastraße 37 facility does not feature a walk-in daily exhibition; the historical archive, research library, and collections are accessible to researchers and interested visitors by advance appointment (Mon–Fri via museum@alpenverein.at). By public transport: from Innsbruck Hauptbahnhof take tram line 3 or bus T/J to Olympiaworld (approx. 5 min). By car: Inntalautobahn A12, exit Innsbruck Ost/Mitte.

Tips

The modern headquarters in Olympiastraße 37 is fully barrier-free. Check the museum website for details on current traveling exhibitions across Austria.
